precedence: 1. Explicit directed GTFS transfers.txt rule for (from_stop_id, to_stop_id)
2. Same physical platform (from_stop_id == to_stop_id with explicit platform suffix): tau_same_platform_seconds (default 90s; sensitivity grid [60, 90, 120])
3. Parent-station fallback min_transfer_time when platform assignment is absent or cross-platform pair is unlisted
transfer_time_contract.retired_unverifiable_requirement: 2023 Swiss official ist-daten lacks physical track/platform columns (GLEIS/KANTE) and GTFS-RT TripUpdate provides announcements rather than track-circuit occupation; actual_platform_pairs_verified==all is retired and replaced by announced-vs-static stability auditing (99.46% agreement in natural_gap_v2).

metric_c1_initial_availability.scope: Root-level initial vehicle operating status prior to first onboard arrival
metric_c1_initial_availability.treatment: Reported explicitly as pre-onboard service cancellation rate; never mixed as [-1, 1] missingness bounds into conditional onboard transfer calibration.

metric_c2_conditional_onboard_calibratio.scope: All registered upstream-vs-downstream transfer opportunities conditional on reaching the first onboard decision state
metrics: Four-partition empirical minus predicted residuals (P00, P01, P10, P11) with whole-date cluster bootstrap CIs
Four-class Brier score and Brier skill score against schedule-nominal and empirical climatology
Stratified P10 hub-approach delay bias diagnostic (forecast_age, mct_difference, peak_hour)
metric_c2_conditional_onboard_calibratio.retired_broken_gate: Simultaneous +/-0.02 98.75% Bonferroni equivalence on N=14 date clusters is retired because (a) N=14 cluster SE (~0.0055) cannot clear +/-0.02 reliably even at tiny bias, and (b) P10 exhibits a real +2.1% to +4.2% morning-peak hub-throat delay bias that must be modeled or guarded rather than treated as an unpassable binary blocker.

execution_latency_contract.async_wall_clock_accounting: Required for any online controller claim; >5s multi-world rollouts (e.g., 49s full128) are strictly offline Monte Carlo references, not deployable online policies.

center_A_selective_certified_recourse.core_thesis: Decompose real-time transit recourse into (1) data identity & exact-anchor conditioning, (2) prefix-closed candidate completeness, (3) recursive selective waiting, and (4) sub-dwell CI-certified selective tail-race lookahead, proving why 97%+ of urban rail decisions collapse to O(1) selective waiting while isolating and solving the <3% tail-race regime within <2s CPU without uncertified MC noise harms.

center_B_empirical_attribution_and_contr.core_thesis: Establish via large-scale causal replay across 34 Swiss operating days that GTFS-RT trip-identity errors (68% corrupted training updates), station-max transfer penalties (56.5% same-platform transfers), and continuation-value inconsistency dominate online tree search, demonstrating structural near-optimality of lightweight selective waiting in high-frequency corridors.

evaluation_rules.baseline_comparison: Paired comparison against each individual deployable causal baseline (primarily prefix-closed cheap selective waiting and full-graph MeanSnapshotCSA), never against an infeasible post-hoc per-root minimum across six policies.
evaluation_rules.compute_parity: Quality-vs-latency Pareto frontier under real async execution clock; online challenger must satisfy mean CPU <= 2.0s and p99 CPU <= 5.0s.
evaluation_rules.decision_certification: Any stochastic rollout override of the analytical continuation action must satisfy paired CI certification (|mean_gain| - z_alpha * se > margin) so finite-sample MC noise cannot induce systematic regressions.
